podcast.title: Appeared in Weezer's Africa Video
podcast.body: "Weird Al" Yankovic made an appearance in Weezer's music video for their cover of "Africa." This was noted as a distinct difference from Toto's original video for the song. "Although I don't remember weird Al being in the original back in the early 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Backmasking Use (70s/80s)
podcast.body: "Weird Al" Yankovic utilized backmasking effects in his music during the 1970s and 1980s, which was a peak era for the technique. "Tons of artists used back masking effects in the 70s and 80s. That seems to be when things reached their peak. Iron Maiden, Pink Floyd, Sticks, Prince B-52s, Weird Al, they were all into it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Defined as Novelty Artist
podcast.body: "Weird Al" Yankovic is explicitly named as an artist considered to be a novelty artist. "Weird out. That's who I consider to be a novelty artist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Music Video Direction by Liam Lynch
podcast.body: Liam Lynch directed music videos for "Weird Al" Yankovic. "He went on to direct music videos for... Weird L."

podcast.title: Pentium Chip Song
podcast.body: Weird Al Yankovic composed a song that referenced the powerful Pentium computer chips introduced by Intel. This detail illustrates the significant cultural impact and widespread recognition that Pentium computers achieved during the 1990s. "Even Weird Al wrote a song about them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall of the MP3

podcast.title: Sweet-Natured Parodies
podcast.body: Weird Al Yankovic is generally associated with parodies that are sweet-natured rather than acting as diss records. He typically avoids creating beef records due to a preference for less mean-spirited content. "Parity is a word we normally associate with the likes of Weird Al Yankovic, whose parodies are usually sweet-natured, not disc records per se."

podcast.title: Unique Position in Nerd Rock
podcast.body: "Weird Al" Yankovic is described as occupying his own unique and prominent position within the nerd rock world, highlighting his significant and distinct contribution to the genre. "And Weird Alienka that who occupies his own throne in the nerd rock world."
